subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow Feishu bug fix; it creates durable agents, workspaces, skills, config, memory namespaces, and message-routing authority from group-chat senders.

options.title: Design Generic Contract First
options.body: Create an admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and shared/private memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

options.title: Keep Session-Only Routing
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope and explicit thread-bound subagent mechanisms, documenting that full per-user orchestration is external deployment architecture for now.

options.title: Reject Automatic Provisioning
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide group-chat identities should not create durable OpenClaw agents automatically.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Contract First
recommendation.body: Create an admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and shared/private memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across Feishu routing, docs, plugin state, and current channel-extension direction.
